records.source: וַיַּ֤עַשׂ אָסָא֙ הַטּ֣וֹב וְהַיָּשָׁ֔ר בְּעֵינֵ֖י יְהוָ֥ה אֱלֹהָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And did Asa the good and the right in [the] eyes of Yahweh his God.
pieces: Asa did what was good and right in the sight of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.

L.1: And Asa did the good and the right in [the] eyes of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God.

R.1: Asa did what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God said was good and right.

decisions.choice: verse numbers: the Hebrew text begins chapter 14 here
decisions.reason: This translation numbers verses as the Hebrew text does. In the Hebrew text chapter 13 ends with the note that the land was quiet for ten years (13:23 here), and this verse begins chapter 14. Many Bibles number that note 14:1, and so number this chapter's verses (14:1-14 here) 14:2-15. The words are the same; only the numbers differ.

decisions.choice: the good and the right in the eyes of Yahweh his God: the good verdict of 1 Kings 15:11, enlarged
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 15:11 says that Asa did "the right" in Yahweh's eyes, "like David his father". Chronicles adds "the good" and "his God", and leaves out the comparison with David. The verdict stands at the head of Asa's reign and is filled out by what follows: his reforms (verses 2-4), his building (verses 5-6) and his trust in Yahweh in battle (verse 10).

decisions.choice: did the good and the right in [the] eyes of / did what was good and right in the sight of / did what the LORD his God said was good and right
decisions.reason: The wording of the good verdict at each level, as in 1 Kings 15:11, with "good" added where Chronicles adds it.

records.heading: Asa king of Judah

records.source: וַיָּ֛סַר אֶת־מִזְבְּח֥וֹת הַנֵּכָ֖ר וְהַבָּמ֑וֹת וַיְשַׁבֵּר֙ אֶת־הַמַּצֵּב֔וֹת וַיְגַדַּ֖ע אֶת־הָאֲשֵׁרִֽים׃
records.gloss: And he removed altars of the foreign and the high places, and he broke the standing stones, and he cut down the Asherah poles.
pieces: He took away the foreign altars and the high places, smashed the standing stones and cut down the Asherah poles.

L.2: And he removed the altars of the foreign [gods] and the high places, and he broke the standing stones and cut down the Asherah poles.

R.2: He got rid of the altars to foreign gods and the hilltop shrines. He smashed the stone pillars and cut down the poles used to worship Asherah.

decisions.choice: altars of the foreign: altars for the worship of foreign gods
decisions.reason: The phrase is "altars of foreignness". The same word names "the foreign gods" Jacob's household put away (Genesis 35:2) and those Israel put away in Judges 10:16; here it describes altars set up to such gods.

decisions.choice: high places, standing stones, Asherah poles: the places and objects of local and foreign worship
decisions.reason: The high places were local places of worship, often on hills. The standing stones were upright stones set up as sacred markers, and the Asherah poles were wooden poles standing for the goddess Asherah. The law commanded Israel to break such stones and cut down such poles (Deuteronomy 7:5; 12:3), with the same two verbs used here.

decisions.choice: Asa's reform as Chronicles tells it
decisions.reason: 1 Kings 15:12 says that Asa drove out the male shrine prostitutes and removed the idols his fathers had made. Chronicles names other things he removed. On the high places, compare verse 4 with 15:17 and 1 Kings 15:14, which say the high places were not taken away.

decisions.choice: high places, standing stones, Asherah poles (Literal, Balanced); hilltop shrines, stone pillars, poles used to worship Asherah (Readable)
decisions.reason: The wording kept for these words in Samuel, Kings and Chronicles. Literal brackets "gods", which the Hebrew implies.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר֙ לִֽיהוּדָ֔ה לִדְר֕וֹשׁ אֶת־יְהוָ֖ה אֱלֹהֵ֣י אֲבוֹתֵיהֶ֑ם וְלַעֲשׂ֖וֹת הַתּוֹרָ֥ה וְהַמִּצְוָֽה׃
records.gloss: And he said to Judah to seek Yahweh [the] God of their fathers and to do the law and the commandment.
pieces: He commanded Judah to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their ancestors, and to carry out the law and its commands.

L.3: And he told Judah to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, the God of their fathers, and to do the law and the commandment.

R.3: He ordered the people of Judah to seek {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, who was the God of their ancestors, and to obey the law and its commands.

decisions.choice: seek Yahweh: turn to him in worship, trust and obedience
decisions.reason: In Chronicles, to seek Yahweh means more than asking him for guidance: it is to turn to him with one's whole life (see the note at 1 Chronicles 10:14). It is the thread of Asa's story: verse 6 says it twice, and 15:2, 12-13 return to it.

decisions.choice: he said to Judah to seek: he commanded them
decisions.reason: "Said" followed by "to" and a verb gives an order (as 1 Chronicles 21:17).

decisions.choice: the law and the commandment: the whole of what Yahweh had commanded
decisions.reason: Both words are singular, standing for the whole body of God's instruction given through Moses and all that it commands.

decisions.choice: commanded / ordered; carry out / obey; its commands
decisions.reason: The verb "said" with "to seek" is an order (m2). The singular "commandment" is collective, so Balanced and Readable say "its commands".

records.source: וַיָּ֨סַר֙ מִכָּל־עָרֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֔ה אֶת־הַבָּמ֖וֹת וְאֶת־הַֽחַמָּנִ֑ים וַתִּשְׁקֹ֥ט הַמַּמְלָכָ֖ה לְפָנָֽיו׃
records.gloss: And he removed from all [the] cities of Judah the high places and the incense altars; and was quiet the kingdom before him.
pieces: He removed the high places and the incense altars from all the cities of Judah, and the kingdom had peace under him.

L.4: And he removed from all the cities of Judah the high places and the incense altars; and the kingdom was quiet before him.

R.4: He took the hilltop shrines and the incense altars away from all the towns of Judah. While he ruled, the kingdom had peace.

decisions.choice: incense altars: small altars, probably for burning incense to other gods
decisions.reason: The word is rare, and its meaning is not certain. Small stone altars for incense have been found in the region, and the word may be linked with one of these; others connect it with a word for the sun, giving "sun pillars". Whatever their shape, they were objects of false worship (Leviticus 26:30; Isaiah 17:8; Ezekiel 6:4, 6).

decisions.choice: removed the high places from the cities of Judah
decisions.reason: 15:17 and 1 Kings 15:14 say that the high places were not removed. 15:17 says this of "Israel", which may mean the northern towns Asa held; or Asa's removal may not have lasted. The text gives both statements without resolving them.

decisions.choice: the kingdom was quiet before him: it was at peace under his rule
decisions.reason: The verb is the one Judges uses for the land's rest after each rescue (Judges 3:11), and the one used in 13:23. "Before him" means while he ruled.

decisions.choice: had peace
decisions.reason: As in Judges, Balanced and Readable say "had peace" for this verb; Literal keeps "was quiet". Readable says "towns", Literal and Balanced "cities".

records.source: וַיִּ֛בֶן עָרֵ֥י מְצוּרָ֖ה בִּיהוּדָ֑ה כִּֽי־שָׁקְטָ֣ה הָאָ֗רֶץ וְאֵין־עִמּ֤וֹ מִלְחָמָה֙ בַּשָּׁנִ֣ים הָאֵ֔לֶּה כִּֽי־הֵנִ֥יחַ יְהוָ֖ה לֽוֹ׃
records.gloss: And he built cities of fortification in Judah, for was quiet the land, and there [was] not with him war in the years the these, for had given rest Yahweh to him.
pieces: He built fortified cities in Judah, since the land had peace. No one went to war with him in those years, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given him rest.

L.5: And he built fortified cities in Judah, for the land was quiet, and there was no war with him in those years, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given him rest.

R.5: He built cities with strong walls in Judah, because the land had peace. During those years no one fought against him, because {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} had given him rest.

decisions.choice: Yahweh had given him rest: the peace was Yahweh's gift
decisions.reason: Rest from enemies is what Yahweh promised Israel in the land (Deuteronomy 12:10) and gave to David and Solomon (1 Chronicles 22:9, 18). Chronicles ties Asa's peace to his seeking Yahweh (verse 6; 15:15).

decisions.choice: those years: the ten quiet years of 13:23
decisions.reason: The years of peace counted in 13:23, before Zerah's attack (verse 8).

decisions.choice: no one went to war with him / no one fought against him
decisions.reason: "There was no war with him" means he was not attacked; Balanced and Readable say so as a clause with a subject.

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר לִֽיהוּדָ֜ה נִבְנֶ֣ה׀אֶת־הֶעָרִ֣ים הָאֵ֗לֶּה וְנָסֵ֨ב חוֹמָ֣ה וּמִגְדָּלִים֮ דְּלָתַ֣יִם וּבְרִיחִים֒ עוֹדֶ֨נּוּ הָאָ֜רֶץ לְפָנֵ֗ינוּ כִּ֤י דָרַ֨שְׁנוּ֙ אֶת־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהֵ֔ינוּ דָּרַ֕שְׁנוּ וַיָּ֥נַֽח לָ֖נוּ מִסָּבִ֑יב וַיִּבְנ֖וּ וַיַּצְלִֽיחוּ׃פ
records.gloss: And he said to Judah, Let us build the cities the these and surround [them with] wall and towers, doors [and] bars; still it the land [is] before us, because we have sought Yahweh our God; we have sought, and he has given rest to us from around. And they built and prospered.
pieces: He said to Judah, "Let us build these cities and put walls around them, with towers, gates and bars. The land is still ours, for we have sought {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. We sought {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave us rest all around." So they built, and they prospered.

L.6: And he said to Judah, "Let us build these cities and surround [them with] wall and towers, doors and bars. The land is still before us, because we have sought {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God; we have sought [{{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}], and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave us rest all around." And they built and prospered.

R.6: He said to the people of Judah, "Let us build up these cities. Let us put walls around them, with towers and gates that can be barred shut. The land still belongs to us. That is because we have sought {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} our God. We went looking for {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} gave us peace from the enemies all around us." So they built the cities and did well.

decisions.choice: the land is still before us: it is still ours, open to us
decisions.reason: "Before us" means at our disposal, as when Abimelech tells Abraham "my land is before you" (Genesis 20:15). While there is peace and the land is in their hands, they can build.

decisions.choice: we have sought [him]: the verb is repeated for emphasis
decisions.reason: The Hebrew repeats "we have sought" with no object. The ancient Greek translation appears to read the second verb as "he has sought us", which would make Yahweh's answer match their seeking. The Hebrew as it stands is followed here.

decisions.choice: wall and towers, doors and bars: a city's defenses
decisions.reason: A fortified city had a wall with towers, and gates of double doors held shut by bars across them (Deuteronomy 3:5; 2 Chronicles 8:5).

decisions.choice: prospered: they succeeded in what they did
decisions.reason: The verb means to succeed or do well; in Chronicles it often follows obedience (1 Chronicles 22:13; 2 Chronicles 31:21).

decisions.choice: gates (Balanced, Readable); the land is still ours / still belongs to us
decisions.reason: The "doors" of a city are its gates. Balanced and Readable say plainly what "the land is before us" means (m1).

decisions.choice: gave us peace from the enemies all around us
decisions.reason: Readable says what "rest all around" means: no enemy around them was at war with them.

records.source: וַיְהִ֣י לְאָסָ֗א חַיִל֮ נֹשֵׂ֣א צִנָּ֣ה וָרֹמַח֒ מִֽיהוּדָה֙ שְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֣וֹת אֶ֔לֶףסוּמִבִּנְיָמִ֗ן נֹשְׂאֵ֤י מָגֵן֙ וְדֹ֣רְכֵי קֶ֔שֶׁת מָאתַ֥יִם וּשְׁמוֹנִ֖ים אָ֑לֶף כָּל־אֵ֖לֶּה גִּבּ֥וֹרֵי חָֽיִל׃
records.gloss: And was to Asa an army carrying large shield and spear, from Judah three hundred thousand, and from Benjamin carrying shield and drawing bow two hundred and eighty thousand; all these [were] mighty [men] of valor.
pieces: Asa had an army of 300,000 men from Judah, armed with large shields and spears, and 280,000 from Benjamin, who carried small shields and drew the bow. All of them were mighty warriors.

L.7: And Asa had an army carrying large shield and spear: from Judah 300,000; and from Benjamin, carrying shield and drawing bow, 280,000. All these [were] mighty men of valor.

R.7: Asa had an army of 300,000 men from Judah, who carried large shields and spears. He also had 280,000 men from Benjamin, who carried small shields and shot with bows. All of them were brave warriors.

decisions.choice: large shield and spear; shield and bow: two kinds of troops
decisions.reason: The first word names a large shield that covered the whole body, carried with a spear by soldiers who fought in close ranks. The second names a smaller round shield, carried by archers. Benjamin was known for its bowmen and slingers (1 Chronicles 12:2).

decisions.choice: thousand: the numbers as given
decisions.reason: On the size of numbers given in thousands, see the note at Numbers 1:21; here, as there, the text is read as giving the number.

decisions.choice: mighty men of valor: tried and able fighting men
decisions.reason: The phrase names strong, capable warriors, as in 13:3.

decisions.choice: men
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable add "men" to the totals.

records.heading: Victory over Zerah the Cushite

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֨א אֲלֵיהֶ֜ם זֶ֣רַח הַכּוּשִׁ֗י בְּחַ֨יִל֙ אֶ֣לֶף אֲלָפִ֔ים וּמַרְכָּב֖וֹת שְׁלֹ֣שׁ מֵא֑וֹת וַיָּבֹ֖א עַד־מָרֵשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And came out against them Zerah the Cushite with an army [of] a thousand thousands and chariots three hundred, and he came to Mareshah.
pieces: Zerah the Cushite marched out against them with an army of a million men and 300 chariots, and he came as far as Mareshah.

L.8: And Zerah the Cushite came out against them with an army of a thousand thousands and 300 chariots, and he came as far as Mareshah.

R.8: Then Zerah the Cushite came out to fight them. He had an army of a million men and 300 chariots. He came as far as the town of Mareshah.

decisions.choice: Zerah the Cushite: a leader from Cush or of Cushite people
decisions.reason: Cush was the land south of Egypt, on the upper Nile. Zerah is not named outside this account, and the text does not say whether he led an army for Egypt or a band of Cushites settled in the south near Gerar (verse 12; 21:16). Verse 13 and 16:8 show that his force included many people and much livestock.

decisions.choice: a thousand thousands: a vast army
decisions.reason: The number is the largest army in Chronicles. On numbers given in thousands, see verse 7; here the point is that Asa's army faced one much larger, which is what his prayer says (verse 10).

decisions.choice: Mareshah: a town in the low hills of western Judah
decisions.reason: Rehoboam had fortified it (11:8). Zerah had come up from the south-west into Judah's own territory.

decisions.choice: a million men
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "a million" for "a thousand thousands" and add "men". Readable adds "the town of".

records.source: וַיֵּצֵ֥א אָסָ֖א לְפָנָ֑יו וַיַּֽעַרְכוּ֙ מִלְחָמָ֔ה בְּגֵ֥יא צְפַ֖תָה לְמָרֵשָֽׁה׃
records.gloss: And went out Asa before him, and they drew up battle in [the] valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.
pieces: Asa went out to meet him, and they took up their positions for battle in the Valley of Zephathah near Mareshah.

L.9: And Asa went out before him, and they drew up [the] battle in the valley of Zephathah at Mareshah.

R.9: Asa went out to face him. The armies lined up for battle in the Zephathah Valley near Mareshah.

decisions.choice: went out before him: went out to meet him in battle
decisions.reason: To go out "before" an enemy is to go out to face him.

decisions.choice: they drew up the battle: the armies formed their battle lines
decisions.reason: The verb means to set in order; with "battle" it means to take up battle positions (1 Chronicles 19:9-10). "They" may be both armies or Asa's men.

decisions.choice: the valley of Zephathah
decisions.reason: The place is not named elsewhere. The ancient Greek translation reads "in the valley north of Mareshah", as if from a very similar Hebrew word. The Hebrew text is followed here.

decisions.choice: went out to meet / to face; took up their positions / lined up
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what the idioms mean (m1, m2).

records.source: וַיִּקְרָ֨א אָסָ֜א אֶל־יְהוָ֣ה אֱלֹהָיו֮ וַיֹּאמַר֒ יְהוָ֗ה אֵֽין־עִמְּךָ֤ לַעְזוֹר֙ בֵּ֥ין רַב֙ לְאֵ֣ין כֹּ֔חַ עָזְרֵ֜נוּ יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ כִּֽי־עָלֶ֣יךָ נִשְׁעַ֔נּוּ וּבְשִׁמְךָ֣ בָ֔אנוּ עַל־הֶהָמ֖וֹן הַזֶּ֑ה יְהוָ֤ה אֱלֹהֵ֨ינוּ֙ אַ֔תָּה אַל־יַעְצֹ֥ר עִמְּךָ֖ אֱנֽוֹשׁ׃ס
records.gloss: And called Asa to Yahweh his God and said, Yahweh, there is not with you to help between great and to no strength; help us, Yahweh our God, for on you we lean, and in your name we have come against the multitude the this. Yahweh, our God [are] you; let not retain [strength] with you man.
pieces: Then Asa cried out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God: "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, there is no one but {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to help when the weak stand against the strong. Help us, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, because we are depending on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}; it is in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name that we have marched out against this huge army. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are our God. Let no mortal hold out against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

L.10: And Asa called to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God and said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, there is none with {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} to help between the mighty and the one without strength. Help us, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God, for we lean on {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}, and in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name we have come against this multitude. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} [are] our God; let not man prevail against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

R.10: Then Asa called out to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} his God. He said, "{{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, when the weak face the strong, only {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} can help them. Help us, {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}} our God! We are trusting in {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}. We have come out in {{deity_pronoun:your|Your}} name to fight this huge army. {{divine_name:LORD|Yahweh}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}} are our God. Do not let mere humans win against {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}."

decisions.choice: there is none with you to help between the mighty and the powerless: no one but Yahweh can help the weak against the strong
alternatives: for you it makes no difference whether you help the mighty or the powerless
there is none like you to help
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is compressed and hard. Read one way, it says that only Yahweh can come between a strong attacker and a weak defender to help. Read another way, it says that with Yahweh it is all the same to help the strong or the weak, as Jonathan said that nothing keeps Yahweh from saving "by many or by few" (1 Samuel 14:6). Both readings make the same point for Asa: his small army can win because Yahweh helps. Literal keeps the Hebrew's shape.

decisions.choice: we lean on you: we rely on you
decisions.reason: The verb means to lean or rest one's weight on something. It is the word used of Judah's victory in 13:18, and the prophet Hanani recalls this battle with it in 16:7-8, when Asa later relied on the king of Aram instead.

decisions.choice: in your name: as yours, trusting in you and acting for you
decisions.reason: To come "in the name" of Yahweh is to come under his authority and depending on him (1 Samuel 17:45).

decisions.choice: let not man prevail against you: do not let a mere mortal stand against you
decisions.reason: The word for man stresses human weakness. The verb means to hold back or keep strength. Asa treats the battle as Yahweh's own: if Zerah wins, a human has prevailed over God.

decisions.choice: when the weak stand against the strong / when the weak face the strong
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable follow the first reading of the hard clause (m1) and put it in plain words; the footnote gives the other.

decisions.choice: depending on / trusting in; huge army; mortal / mere humans
decisions.reason: "Lean on" means to rely (m2). The "multitude" is Zerah's army (verse 8). Readable says "win against" for the verb "prevail".

records.source: וַיִּגֹּ֤ף יְהוָה֙ אֶת־הַכּוּשִׁ֔ים לִפְנֵ֥י אָסָ֖א וְלִפְנֵ֣י יְהוּדָ֑ה וַיָּנֻ֖סוּ הַכּוּשִֽׁים׃
records.gloss: And struck Yahweh the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and fled the Cushites.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} struck down the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.

L.11: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} struck the Cushites before Asa and before Judah, and the Cushites fled.

R.11: So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} defeated the Cushites in front of Asa and the people of Judah, and the Cushites ran away.

decisions.choice: Yahweh struck the Cushites: the victory is his
decisions.reason: The verb means to strike or defeat. Yahweh is its subject, not Asa: the answer to the prayer of verse 10. 13:15 tells Abijah's victory the same way.

decisions.choice: before Asa and before Judah: in front of them, while they faced the enemy
decisions.reason: Judah's army was there and fought (verse 12), but the blow came from Yahweh.

decisions.choice: struck down / defeated
decisions.reason: Balanced keeps the picture of a blow; Readable says what it meant.

records.source: וַיִּרְדְּפֵ֨ם אָסָ֜א וְהָעָ֣ם אֲשֶׁר־עִמּוֹ֮ עַד־לִגְרָר֒ וַיִּפֹּ֤ל מִכּוּשִׁים֙ לְאֵ֣ין לָהֶ֣ם מִֽחְיָ֔ה כִּֽי־נִשְׁבְּר֥וּ לִפְנֵֽי־יְהוָ֖ה וְלִפְנֵ֣י מַחֲנֵ֑הוּ וַיִּשְׂא֥וּ שָׁלָ֖ל הַרְבֵּ֥ה מְאֹֽד׃
records.gloss: And pursued them Asa and the people who [were] with him to Gerar, and fell of [the] Cushites until there was not to them recovery, for they were broken before Yahweh and before his camp; and they carried off plunder very much.
pieces: Asa and the troops with him chased them as far as Gerar. So many Cushites fell that they could not recover; they were shattered before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} army. The men of Judah carried off a great deal of plunder.

L.12: And Asa and the people who [were] with him pursued them as far as Gerar, and of the Cushites [so many] fell that they had no recovery, for they were broken before {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} and before {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} camp. And they carried off very much plunder.

R.12: Asa and his army chased them all the way to Gerar. So many Cushites were killed that their army could not recover. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} and {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} army had crushed them. The army of Judah took away a huge amount of plunder.

decisions.choice: there was no recovery for them: they could not regroup
alternatives: none of them was left alive
decisions.reason: The word means keeping alive or recovering. It may mean that the Cushite army was broken past rallying, or that none of them survived. The first fits the size of the army and the flight already told (verse 11).

decisions.choice: before Yahweh and his camp: Judah's army as Yahweh's army
alternatives: before Yahweh and before Asa's camp
decisions.reason: "His" most naturally refers to Yahweh, named just before: Judah's army fought as Yahweh's own host (compare "the camp of God", 1 Chronicles 12:23). It could also refer to Asa.

decisions.choice: Gerar: a town in the south-west, toward Philistia
decisions.reason: Gerar lay in the western Negev, between Gaza and Beersheba (Genesis 20:1; 26:1). The pursuit went far beyond Mareshah, out of Judah.

decisions.choice: the troops (Balanced); his army (Readable)
decisions.reason: "The people" here is the army in the field; Literal keeps "the people".

decisions.choice: the men of Judah / the army of Judah
decisions.reason: The Hebrew says only "they carried off"; Balanced and Readable name Judah's men so the reader does not take the Cushites as the subject.

records.source: וַיַּכּ֗וּ אֵ֤ת כָּל־הֶֽעָרִים֙ סְבִיב֣וֹת גְּרָ֔ר כִּי־הָיָ֥ה פַֽחַד־יְהוָ֖ה עֲלֵיהֶ֑ם וַיָּבֹ֨זּוּ֙ אֶת־כָּל־הֶ֣עָרִ֔ים כִּֽי־בִזָּ֥ה רַבָּ֖ה הָיְתָ֥ה בָהֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And they struck all the cities around Gerar, for was [the] dread of Yahweh on them; and they plundered all the cities, for much plunder was in them.
pieces: They attacked all the cities around Gerar, for the dread of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} lay on them. They plundered all those cities, since there was a great deal of plunder in them.

L.13: And they struck all the cities around Gerar, for the dread of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was on them; and they plundered all the cities, for there was much plunder in them.

R.13: They attacked all the towns around Gerar. The people there were terrified of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Judah's army took everything of value from those towns, because there was so much to take.

decisions.choice: the dread of Yahweh was on them: a terror from Yahweh kept them from resisting
decisions.reason: The phrase names a fear that God himself sends on enemies, so that they do not fight (Genesis 35:5; 2 Chronicles 17:10; 20:29). "Them" is the people of the towns.

decisions.choice: the cities around Gerar: towns linked with Zerah's force
decisions.reason: The text does not say why they were attacked; they were most likely allied with the Cushites or gave them a base.

decisions.choice: the people there; Judah's army
decisions.reason: Readable names who was afraid and who plundered, which the Hebrew leaves to "them" and "they".

records.source: וְגַם־אָהֳלֵ֥י מִקְנֶ֖ה הִכּ֑וּ וַיִּשְׁבּ֨וּ צֹ֤אן לָרֹב֙ וּגְמַלִּ֔ים וַיָּשֻׁ֖בוּ יְרוּשָׁלִָֽם׃ס
records.gloss: And also tents of livestock they struck, and they took captive sheep in abundance and camels, and they returned [to] Jerusalem.
pieces: They also attacked the herders' camps and carried off sheep and goats in great numbers, and camels. Then they returned to Jerusalem.

L.14: And they also struck the tents of livestock, and carried off flocks in abundance, and camels; and they returned [to] Jerusalem.

R.14: They also attacked the camps of the people who kept herds. They took away large numbers of sheep, goats and camels. Then they went back to Jerusalem.

decisions.choice: tents of livestock: the camps of herdsmen
decisions.reason: The tents of people who lived with their herds, moving with the grazing. The Hebrew names them by what they owned.

decisions.choice: flocks: sheep and goats together
decisions.reason: The word names a flock of small livestock, sheep and goats.

decisions.choice: carried off: took as captives
decisions.reason: The verb is used for taking prisoners of war; here it is used of the animals driven away as spoil.

decisions.choice: the herders' camps / the camps of the people who kept herds; sheep and goats
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say whose tents these were (m1) and what the flocks were (m2).
